added 64 commits

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19926/diffs?diff_id=1364667497&start_sha=8b9c796ca26050b34264ebeed354a0776ae15fa5)
I think we would like default black foreground color in light mode.

I'm not sure, it seems that the affected colors are not dependent on the light/dark mode:

![Wireshark_Preferences_dark_light](/uploads/f3c71ce24f29a54d51d20be9408412c6/Wireshark_Preferences_dark_light.png)

Maybe we need some more logic, on macOS it's different.
![Screenshot_2025-05-21_at_14.50.49](/uploads/87afaac606be21f010279df8eb895872/Screenshot_2025-05-21_at_14.50.49.png)

As a reference, dark mode looks good.
![Screenshot_2025-05-21_at_15.09.36](/uploads/de20aef0574c37fc0ddd4dc77d5b0bcb/Screenshot_2025-05-21_at_15.09.36.png)

Okay, I see this doesn't look so good.
There seems to be something wrong with the way the background color is set in Windows light mode (at least for me...). The code only distinguishes between light and dark, and not (at least not obviously) by platform.
I'll take another look. In my opinion, the default should behave as shown in your screenshots.
It may not be (just) a Windows vs MacOS issue, as the color scheme handling related to dark mode has seen a lot of changes in recent Qt releases. What versions are you building and running against?

Yes, that was my mistake ;-)
I was still using a version of Qt before 6.8 in my setup. Apparently, the internal detection of the set mode wasn't working (correctly) – it was always dark, even if the interface was set to light.
I switched my setup to Qt 6.9. Now the mode detection works correctly, and I have the same (unsightly) default color combination as on a Mac.
I'm still adjusting the default text color, depending on the mode.

The default colors should now look better

Should be done

Good. Now you need to fix the commit subject and message. The Issue fixed should be moved from the commit subject to last line in the commit message. Also, it looks like the commit message is repeated 3 times.

It looks like something happened in your rebase/squash. The author and date is copied from a different commit.
```
Author:     Cal Turney <cturney111@gmail.com>
AuthorDate: Wed May 21 18:20:56 2025 -0400
Commit:     Michael C. Oed <2123595-michaeloed@users.noreply.gitlab.com>
CommitDate: Fri May 23 15:08:25 2025 +0200

    Adding support for changing foreground color in filter edit
    
    Fixes #20202
```
That's strange if that's wrong... I tried to follow the instructions in chapter 3.10.5 of the Developer Guide, also because I've only just started to get to grips with Git.
No problem, you can fix this locally using `git commit --amend --author="Your Name <your@email.com>" --date=now`.
Thanks for the tip and your patience. Things should be better now ;-)

Separately, and not part of this change, there's still the issue that initial values for the filter preferences are chosen based on light mode vs dark mode, but as soon as someone actually sets the preference to a non-default value, the set value is used for both light mode and dark mode. That's not great for people who sometimes run in Light Mode and sometimes in Dark Mode (perhaps on some kind of automatic schedule.) Perhaps ideally there should be two sets of preferences, one for when in light mode and one for when in dark mode.
The backgrounds don't change when dark mode is changed on the fly. Having separate sets of preferences would also make it easier to handle that (and still have preferences.)

@johnthacker We had similar discussions for the Coloring Rules, but didn't conclude on a solution. I had an idea that the UI table could have two tabs with the same content, one for Light and one for Dark. The default selected tab depends on selected mode. Similar could apply for this colors.

Also, still separate from this change, the filter ComboBox is not updated when switching between modes. Automatic scheduled switch is already found on macOS.

> Also, still separate from this change, the filter ComboBox is not updated when switching between modes. Automatic scheduled switch is already found on macOS.

Yes, I saw that. The switch needs to happen on all OSes (!19948), but that only changes the drop down triangle, not the background colors. At least this change is slightly better in that regard because it avoids having the foreground text color change to something unreadable because the background colors don't change.
I agree, this change is good.
